intended_object: For a ring R, a two-sided ideal I and any index type ι, the canonical R/I-linear isomorphism (R^ι)/(I^ι) ≅ (R/I)^ι, sending the class of f to (i ↦ f(i) mod I). This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The forward map sends the class of f to the function i ↦ [f i]. It is well defined because f − g ∈ I^ι exactly when f i − g i ∈ I for every i. The inverse picks a representative of each coordinate's class. Both maps are as expected, and the result is linear over R/I, which is the structure the docstring states.

The generality is natural. R can be any (possibly noncommutative) ring, as long as I is two-sided; that is needed for R/I to be a ring. The index type ι is arbitrary, not just finite. This is not just one case of a general construction that already exists. `Submodule.quotientPi` is a more general isomorphism of quotients of products of modules, but it requires `Fintype ι` and is only R-linear, whereas this definition is R/I-linear and allows any ι. So the definition is neither incorrect nor too narrow.
